sections.heading: 00 — README
sections.intro:
**Polymer Ph.D. — Healthy Baked Goods knowledge package**

This folder contains a synthesised knowledge base built from **Instagram recipe reels**,
one at a time, from many different creators — there is no single channel or author behind
this library.

---

sections.heading: What this is
sections.intro:
**This package synthesises individual Instagram recipe posts, each treated as its own,
independent source.** Every claim in it traces back to a specific post's caption, comments,
or on-screen/spoken content, at a specific paragraph or timestamp.

**Nothing in this package originates outside the source posts.** A recipe's ingredient
list, method, and any substitution notes are exactly what the creator stated — including
their own hedges ("I haven't tried this, but...").

---

sections.heading: What was processed
sections.intro:
| Measure | Figure |
|---|---|
| Recipes written up as structured notes | **1** |
| Source platform | **Instagram (reels)** |
| Knowledge files in this package | **2** (this README and the glossary) |

---

sections.heading: The files
sections.intro:
| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| **`00_README.md`** | This file |
| **`07_PLAIN_ENGLISH_GLOSSARY.md`** | Any technical baking terms the notes introduce, defined in plain language, no citations |
| **`09_SOURCE_CATALOG.md`** | Every recipe — ID, title, creator, URL, upload date, facets. **Generated mechanically from the notes**, so it stays complete as more videos are added |

A fuller synthesis — cross-cutting substitution guidance, an ingredient-by-ingredient
reference, patterns across creators — is deliberately not written yet. With only one note
from one creator, that kind of synthesis would mostly restate one note's own words; per
this project's standing practice, whether to add it is a judgement call revisited as more
recipes are added, not a gap to paper over now.

---

sections.heading: What the package covers
sections.intro:
- **Individual recipes exactly as one creator presented them** — ingredients, method, and
  any stated substitutions or variations.

sections.heading: What the package does not cover
sections.intro:
- **Nutrition analysis.** No note states macro or calorie figures unless the creator
  themselves stated one; nothing here is calculated or estimated.
- **A single creator's point of view, presented as consensus.** Each note is one creator's
  own recipe and claims — conflicting or overlapping recipes from other creators are noted
  in each note's own `## Conflicts with other sources` section as they're added.

---

sections.heading: Upload guidance
sections.intro:
Upload the files in this folder to a Custom GPT's knowledge base, following the same
pattern used for this project's other libraries — see `PASTE_INTO_GPT_INSTRUCTIONS.txt`
for the system prompt.

**Suggested setting:** turn web browsing **off**, so the GPT answers from these sources
rather than the open internet.

---

**A one-bowl, brownie-textured (not cakey) lemon bar, where creaming the butter and sugar
— rather than melting the butter, as an actual brownie would — is what the creator
identifies as the fix for a too-gooey center in her own recipe testing.**
`` `why-every-lemon-lover-needs-this-brownie-recipe-in-their-life`[¶1] `` "These Lemon
Brownies are soft, fudgy citrus bars finished with a glossy white chocolate lemon glaze.
The best part? The whole thing comes together in one bowl." The Instagram caption gates the
recipe (`[¶1]` "comment COZY and ill DM you the recipe").
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
`` `why-every-lemon-lover-needs-this-brownie-recipe-in-their-life`[¶1] `` — the blog's own
recipe card: granulated sugar (1¼ cups/272g), lemon zest (2 tbsp), unsalted butter
(¾ cup/170g, softened), vanilla extract (1 tsp), lemon extract (1 tsp), lemon juice
(2 tbsp), eggs (2 large), all-purpose flour (1¼ cups/162.5g), baking powder (¾ tsp), kosher
salt (½ tsp). Glaze: white chocolate (¾ cup/113g), lemon juice (2 tbsp), lemon extract
(¼ tsp), salt (pinch), lemon zest (1 tbsp, for garnish).
sections.heading: Ingredients

sections.body:
`` `why-every-lemon-lover-needs-this-brownie-recipe-in-their-life`[¶1] `` Rub the lemon
zest into the sugar by hand to release the oils, then cream in the softened butter, vanilla,
and lemon extract until fluffy. Beat in the lemon juice and eggs, then the flour, baking
powder, and salt — mixing only until combined, since "overmixing can encourage gluten to
form" in this recipe. Bake at 350°F for about 25 minutes. Let cool before glazing: melt the
white chocolate with lemon juice, stir in lemon extract and salt, pour over the cooled bars,
and let set 20 minutes before slicing.
sections.heading: Method

sections.body:
`` `why-every-lemon-lover-needs-this-brownie-recipe-in-their-life`[¶1] `` The blog documents
three explicit test iterations: Test #1 (melted butter and white chocolate mixed into the
batter) was "a solid start" but needed more moisture, lift, and lemon flavor. Test #2 (part
brown sugar, added baking powder, more zest) improved the lemon flavor but turned "too gooey
in the center," and both versions were judged too rich to glaze. Test #3 — creaming butter
and sugar instead of melting, and moving the white chocolate out of the batter and into a
glaze — is the version given above.

Framed as a spring/warm-weather dessert alternative to a chocolate brownie —
`` `why-every-lemon-lover-needs-this-brownie-recipe-in-their-life`[¶1] `` "where chocolate
brownies feel more late-night, these feel more daytime." No dietary restriction is claimed.

**A standard banana quick bread studded with diced fresh strawberries — never frozen, by
the creator's explicit instruction — and topped with a cream cheese frosting whose
concentrated strawberry flavor comes from blitzed freeze-dried strawberries rather than
fresh purée.** `[¶1]` "strawberries and cream banana bread 🍓🍌 inspired by wimbledon 🎾🎾."
`` `a-fruity-twist-that-makes-banana-bread-even-better`[¶1] `` "I would only use fresh
berries here since frozen strawberries can add excess moisture." The Instagram caption
gates the recipe (`[¶1]` "comment COZY and i'll DM you the recipe").
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
`` `a-fruity-twist-that-makes-banana-bread-even-better`[¶1] `` — the blog's own recipe card:
unsalted butter (½ cup, melted), avocado or olive oil (3 tbsp), mashed banana (1⅓
cups/300g), granulated sugar (¾ cup/150g), vanilla (1 tsp), eggs (2 large), baking powder
(1 tsp), baking soda (½ tsp), kosher salt (½ tsp), all-purpose flour (1½ cups/195g), diced
fresh strawberries (1 cup/140g). Frosting: cream cheese (3 oz, room temp), unsalted butter
(4 tbsp, room temp), powdered sugar (1½ cups), freeze-dried strawberries (⅓ cup/8g), heavy
cream (1 tbsp), vanilla extract (½ tsp), kosher salt (pinch).
sections.heading: Ingredients

sections.body:
`` `a-fruity-twist-that-makes-banana-bread-even-better`[¶1] `` Whisk the melted butter, oil,
mashed banana, sugar, vanilla, and eggs, then the baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Fold in the flour just until combined, then fold in the diced strawberries. Bake at 350°F
for 65–75 minutes. Cool at least an hour before frosting — "Even slightly warm banana bread
can cause the cream cheese frosting to melt and slide off." For the frosting: blitz the
freeze-dried strawberries to a powder, beat the cream cheese smooth, beat in the butter,
then the powdered sugar, strawberry powder, salt, vanilla, and heavy cream for a full 2
minutes until fluffy. Swirl over the cooled loaf.

treat — `` `a-fruity-twist-that-makes-banana-bread-even-better`[¶1] `` "simple enough to make
ahead for breakfast, dessert, or an afternoon snack." No dietary restriction is claimed.

**A three-layer bar — buttery crumble base, unbaked sweetened cream cheese, homemade
raspberry jam — topped with more of the same crumble, using one batch of crumble split
between crust and topping.** `[¶1]` "buttery crumble is layered with sweet cream cheese,
homemade raspberry jam (made using frozen raspberries!), and even MORE crumble!" The
Instagram caption gates the written version (`[¶2]` "Comment 'send recipe' and I'll DM it to
you, or find the full recipe on my website!"), fetched here as the second source.
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
`` `raspberry-cheesecake-crumble-bars-butternut-bakery`[¶1] `` — the blog's own recipe card.
Raspberry filling: frozen raspberries (12 oz bag/3 cups), granulated sugar (¼ cup),
cornstarch (1 tbsp), water or lemon juice (2 tbsp). Cream cheese filling: full-fat cream
cheese (12 oz, room temp), granulated sugar (⅓ cup), vanilla extract (1 tsp), egg (1
large). Crumble (used for both crust and topping): light brown sugar (½ cup), granulated
sugar (½ cup), all-purpose flour (2¾ cups), kosher salt (½ tsp), baking powder (1 tsp),
unsalted butter (1 cup, melted and cooled).
sections.heading: Ingredients

sections.body:
`` `raspberry-cheesecake-crumble-bars-butternut-bakery`[¶1] `` Cook the raspberries, sugar,
and cornstarch with water or lemon juice until thick and jammy (5–8 minutes), then chill.
Mash the cream cheese with sugar, then the vanilla and egg, until smooth. Mix the dry
crumble ingredients, stir in the melted butter until evenly moist but still crumbly. Press
about ⅔ of the crumble into the pan as a thin base layer, spread the cream cheese layer
over it, spoon (not pour, to avoid disturbing the cream cheese) the raspberry jam on top,
then break up and scatter the remaining crumble over the surface. Bake at 350°F for 35–40
minutes until the edges are golden and the center barely jiggles. Cool at room temperature
20 minutes, then refrigerate at least 2 hours before slicing into 12 bars.
sections.heading: Method

sections.body:
Positioned as an easy make-ahead centerpiece for a gathering — `` `raspberry-cheesecake-crumble-bars-butternut-bakery`[¶1] ``
"the absolute talk of your next spring or summer event." No dietary restriction is claimed
in the base recipe, though the blog notes a gluten-free swap is possible (§ Source-stated
confidence).

`[¶10]` Preheat to 350°F (180°C) and grease a donut pan. Blend the sweet potato, banana,
egg, maple syrup, milk, oil, and vanilla until smooth; add the dry ingredients and pulse
just until combined — "Avoid continuing to blend once the flour is incorporated." Pipe or
spoon into 8 donut cavities, about ¾ full. Bake 12–15 minutes, until the tops spring back
and a toothpick has a few moist crumbs. Cool in the pan 5–10 minutes, then cool completely
before dipping the tops in the melted chocolate-and-coconut-oil coating.

**An oat-and-almond-flour crumble bar with a cooked cinnamon-apple filling, sandwiched
between two crust layers and topped with a dairy-free caramel made from refrigerated
coconut cream instead of butter and heavy cream.** `[¶3]` "These apple oat bars are so
great to make for breakfast and enjoy throughout the week." The Instagram caption gives an
explicit blog link (`[¶4]` `https://veggieworldrecipes.com/apple-bars/`), fetched here as a
second source; the blog itself states `` `easiest-apple-bars-with-vegan-caramel-sauce`[¶1] ``
"They are vegan and gluten free."
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
`` `easiest-apple-bars-with-vegan-caramel-sauce`[¶1] `` — the blog's own recipe card:

| Component | Ingredients |

| Apple filling | Apples, any kind (3 medium/510g), lemon juice (½ lemon), coconut sugar (⅓ cup), vanilla (½ tsp), cinnamon (1 tsp), cornstarch (2 tbsp) |

sections.heading: Ingredients

sections.body:
`` `easiest-apple-bars-with-vegan-caramel-sauce`[¶1] `` Mix the crust ingredients, press
half into a lined pan as the base layer, reserving the rest for the top. Cook the sliced
apples with lemon juice, cinnamon, coconut sugar, and vanilla for 3–4 minutes, stir in the
cornstarch, then spread the filling over the base crust and top with the remaining crust.
Bake 30–35 minutes at 400°F/200°C. For the caramel: melt the scooped coconut cream solids
with coconut sugar until bubbling, then whisk in vanilla, salt, and cornstarch off the heat;
chill until it thickens before drizzling over the cooled, sliced bars. Makes 9 bars, per
the blog.

sections.body:
Positioned as a make-ahead breakfast/snack bar for the week rather than a special-occasion
dessert. `` `easiest-apple-bars-with-vegan-caramel-sauce`[¶1] `` Both vegan and gluten-free
by ingredient choice (oats, almond flour, coconut oil/sugar/cream — no dairy, eggs, or
wheat flour anywhere in the recipe).
